hypothesis: The TUI process's RSS on a resumed large session (124MB p50 at 10MiB canonical, 396MB at 40MiB, tip 7064d039) is dominated NOT by retained chat data but by (a) the first-frame render churn of the rebuilt transcript's visible window, left in glibc arenas for the process lifetime (the #2872 attach-fold trim runs BEFORE the first frame), and (b) a duplicate copy of every settled assistant message's rendered rows held by the per-entry markdown block cache (md_caches), which exists for streaming replays but is dead weight for settled/resumed messages; additionally scroll walks retain span-fragmented rendered rows for every visited entry forever. Returning the first frame's freed heap + storing settled messages' rows once should cut the TUI process RSS materially with byte-identical rendering.
approach: Two pa-tui edits. (1) session_ui.rs: attach fold arms a one-shot trim_after_frame; interactive.rs consumes it right after the terminal draw gate paints the first frame following the transcript rebuild and calls pa_types::memory_release::trim_freed_heap() (the same call #2872 added at the fold; the render churn happens after it). (2) view.rs render_entry Assistant arm: a still-streaming message keeps the per-entry MarkdownBlockCache (its settled blocks replay per frame); a settled message renders with a throwaway cache and drops any stored copy (rendered rows live once, in the entry layout; any later re-render rebuilds identical rows from the message's own text). Census evidence chain: SIGUSR1-style kick-file census probe build (lane/hillclimb-tui-memory-probe @ be68c20cc/4eee5512f, never ships) walked AgentView state: at 10MiB ready the pad entry held 36,412 layout lines (4.17MB content) + md cache duplicate (key 4.10MB + 36,410 lines) while heights never cache in sparse mode; pre-trim-kick census measured 42MB reclaimable at 10MiB / 132MB at 40MiB ready and post-trim heap ~= census live data; scroll walk (2600 PageUps) added +71.7MB heap = live span-fragmented rows (604k spans for 50k lines) retained after return-to-tail (NOT addressed by this PR; follow-up candidate).
parity_notes: Rendered bytes preserved by construction and by oracle: the throwaway-cache render is the same code path as the cache-miss render (deterministic from the message's own text); pa-tui-replay --frame 120x40 --color dumps on the canonical 10MiB and 40MiB fixtures are BYTE-IDENTICAL base-vs-cand (sha256 48603280488e6c4472033e341273abfa2674d126d77b887bd618545d64404841 and 75cd4390440135e1d0c2ae1187eeea65a87f1c7dddcc10549fc8deaae7a3ff9d, both sides, 4840 bytes each). No wire, schema, prompt, or behavior change: the trim is allocator plumbing (#2872's own helper, non-glibc no-op), the md-cache skip changes only where rendered rows are stored. Interaction parity from the ABBA: resume sentinel time, input echo latency, scroll top-walk time (53.3s both sides), back-walk key count (2750 both sides - identical transcript geometry), and screen evidence (sentinel/task0) are unchanged. The exit-flush inline scrollback write (streaming lane handoff) is untouched; headless render path skips the trim (frame pipelines unchanged).
